newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Carlos the Jackal" denounces French justice.
newsitem.headline: "Carlos the Jackal" denounces French justice.

text.p: Guerrilla "Carlos the Jackal", taking advantage of a routine court hearing on his detention, on Monday questioned the independence and impartiality of France's chief anti-terrorism investigator.
The Venezuelan and his lawyer, Isabelle Coutant-Peyre, refused to attend the hearing at a Paris appeals court on prolonging a custody order issued by investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere.
The order is part of a probe into the December 1983 bombing of the Marseille railway station which killed two people and which Carlos is accused of carrying out.

"Carlos questions the independence and impartiality of Jean-Louis Bruguiere towards him, given the public ties he has with certain civil plaintiffs, notably the SOS Attacks (victims') association," attorney Coutant-Peyre said in a statement.
She said the ties were "too close given the congratulations which this association regularly extends (to Bruguiere) in the press". Her client, she said, denied responsibility for the bombing.

There was no comment immediately available from judicial officials. Bruguiere has in France pioneered briefings with members of the SOS Attacks association to keep victims and their relatives informed of his investigations, although such meetings have not involved cases concerning Carlos.
Carlos, 47, whose real name is Ilich Ramirez Sanchez, has been held in La Sante jail since he was seized in Sudan in 1994 and brought to France.
He is to go on trial for the first time on December 12 for the murder of two French counter-intelligence officers in 1975.
